subject.title: Add loop-aware compaction guard for saturated sessions

question: Should saturated-session loop awareness be added as a new agents.defaults.compaction.guard flow, folded into the existing tools.loopDetection.postCompactionGuard and qualityGuard surfaces, or deferred until a live/sanitized incident fixture proves the policy?
rationale: The remaining work adds config/default surface, runtime compaction policy, validator semantics, and reset recommendations; those choices can affect existing long-session behavior and cannot be settled by source inspection alone.

options.title: Design integrated guard first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the permanent config and reset policy, then update or replace the partial config PR with a narrow implementation backed by a sanitized incident fixture.

options.title: Adopt config-slice PR as the seed
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/48278 as the starting point, but require conflict resolution and explicit follow-up ownership for detector, runtime hook, validator, and reset recommendation behavior.

options.title: Defer until live proof
options.body: Leave current post-compaction and quality guards as-is until a current-main live or sanitized fixture demonstrates the broader saturated-session failure mode.

recommendation.title: Design integrated guard first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers choose the permanent config and reset policy, then update or replace the partial config PR with a narrow implementation backed by a sanitized incident fixture.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent compaction-loop guard follow-up work and current main ownership make this the best available routing candidate for the product/config decision.
